subject: Renewal: utilization-led capacity adjustment and GPU mix recommendation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: utilization-led capacity adjustment and GPU mix recommendation

Hi Sam,

As we approach your Jan 1 renewal, we ran the utilization analysis you requested for NimbusAI's Dedicated fleet. Summary first: based on Q3-Q4 usage patterns and 99th-percentile latency SLO misses tied to high concurrency windows, we recommend adjusting your committed capacity and GPU mix rather than a straight pro-rate top-up.

Quick findings (attached: nimbus-utilization-q3-aggregated.csv):
- Current committed pool: 32 A100 GPUs (migrate path from older V100s completed in Q2).
- Observed steady-state utilization: 62% average across weekdays, 88% during peak windows (09:00–11:00 PST and 18:00–20:00 PST).
- 99th token-latency increases correlate with batch queue depth rising above our optimal 250ms threshold during peaks.

Recommended renewal amendment (business and infra summary):
1) Commit bump: move to 44 total A100-equivalent GPUs (add 12 GPUs). Rationale: target steady-state utilization 55–65% to avoid tail latency degradation and give headroom for burst.
2) Burst buffer: reserve 6 of the added GPUs as a soft burst pool (no additional commit charge unless used >10% of monthly minutes). This preserves cost flexibility.
3) GPU mix: keep A100s for now; if you opt for H100s we can provide a delta-cost analysis — H100s reduce average latency on large-sequence workloads but increase unit cost.
4) Autoscale smoothing: adjust autoscaling cooldowns to 90s and enable small-batch pre-warming for hot prefixes (we've tuned this for Nimbus in the attached config).

Commercially: for the 12-GPU add we can propose a 10% uplift discount on the incremental commit if you sign an annual addendum before Jan 15. Draft amendment attached (redwood-amendment-draft-v2.docx) and HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4491.

Next steps I suggest:
- Share this with your procurement and ops (I included a short appendix in the draft for procurement).
- If you want cost/latency trade-offs, I can run two scenarios (A100-only and A100+H100 hybrid) and return delta TCO.

Happy to walk through over 30 minutes — propose Wed 12/2 10:00–10:30 PST or Thu 12/3 14:00–14:30 PST.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick analysis and the attachments. A couple clarifying questions before we take this to procurement:
1) Can you break down the 12 additional GPUs into expected monthly token-minutes (or cost) at current workload shape? Need to understand spend sensitivity.
2) How does the soft burst buffer work in practice — we want to avoid surprise charges if we hit a traffic storm.
3) Is there an alternative to committing all 12 immediately? e.g., staged 6 now + 6 after Q1 usage review?

Also, latency matters for a key customer pilot scheduled for Feb. If the committed increase is necessary to avoid SLO misses during the pilot, that will sway procurement.

Can you include your operations/engineer who owns the autoscale knobs — we may have some questions about cooldowns and pre-warming.

Appreciate it — Sam

Sam — thanks, good questions. Short answers inline, details below.

On 1) Cost impact: incremental 12 GPUs (A100-equivalent) at Nimbus's current mix ~= +$42k/month raw usage at list; with the 10% incremental discount discussed in the draft, net incremental ~= $37.8k/month. I attached a simple cost sensitivity table in the CSV.

On 2) Soft burst buffer: the burst pool is capacity we keep warm but only bill against committed minutes beyond a 10% free threshold per month. Practically: if you use burst <10% of the monthly minutes it's absorbed; over that we bill incremental minutes at the committed on-demand incremental rate (we can cap monthly incremental spend in the amendment if you like).

On 3) Staged commit: yes — we can stage 6 now and 6 after a 12-week review with objective KPIs (99th latency and queue depth). The staged path preserves a lower upfront cost while giving us runway to observe pilot performance. The draft has a staging clause on pg.2.

Looping in Rishi and Dev for the technical and contracting bits. Rishi — can you add a short note on autoscale/pre-warm defaults and whether the 90s cooldown is safe for Nimbus's traffic profile? Dev — can you confirm procurement flow/timing for the addendum and signatory?

Karthik
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal: utilization-led capacity adjustment and GPU mix recommendation

Hi Sam, Karthik —

Quick ops note from the runtime side:
- Autoscale: 90s cooldown + small-batch pre-warm is conservative and should eliminate the majority of short-tail queue build-ups we've seen. For Nimbus's peak profile I recommend target utilization of 55–65% to keep 99th-token latency comfortably under your SLO.
- KV cache & batching: enabling prefix-focused KV caching for hot models (we identified two high-frequency prefixes in Q3) reduces effective CPU/GPU work during peaks by ~12% in our sim.
- Fallback policy: we'll keep a policy that routes non-critical bulk requests to a lower-cost model variant or an async batch path when queue depth exceeds a configured threshold — this keeps customer-facing latency under control.

On the hardware mix: if you expect more long-sequence (>2k token) workloads during the Feb pilot, H100s give a ~20% latency improvement vs A100 at ~25% higher unit cost. If cost is the priority, A100-only with the reserve burst is a good middle path.

I've attached an updated config snippet (included in the shared Drive link) and a short appendix you can hand to procurement. Dev — can you confirm the staged amendment language and the optional incremental-spend cap?

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Serving & Runtime Optimization | Redwood Inference
